question.problem:
The following table shows the values of a continuous function $f(x)$ over the interval $[1,7].$

| $x$ | $1$ | $2.5$ | $5$ | $7$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $f(x)$ | $3$ | $5$ | $8.5$ | $9$ |

Use the right Riemann sum, with the three subintervals indicated by the data, to approximate the area under the curve $y=f(x)$ over the interval $[1,7].$
question.worked_solution:
In this case, we have $n=3$ rectangles. Using the right Riemann sum, the area is approximated as 

$$
A≈f(2.5)Δ{x}_{1}+f(5)Δ{x}_{2}+f(7)Δ{x}_{3},
$$

where each $Δ{x}_{i}$ is calculated by considering the step between a particular $x$-value and the previous one, i.e.,

$$
Δ{x}_{i}={x}_{i}-{x}_{i-1}.
$$

We set up a value table that includes the $Δx$'s.

| $x$ | $1$ | $2.5$ | $5$ | $7$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $Δx$ | $-$ | $1.5$ | $2.5$ | $2$ |
| $f(x)$ | $-$ | $5$ | $8.5$ | $9$ |

Finally, we plug in the numbers to approximate the area under the curve and get

$$
\begin{aligned}A & ≈5\cdot 1.5+8.5\cdot 2.5+9\cdot 2 \\  & =7.5+21.25+18 \\  & =46.75.\end{aligned}
$$
